sources.title: JORADP n° 31 (2 May 2024): Loi n° 24-07 du 29 avril 2024 relative à l'industrie cinématographique
sources.said: Article 1er. — La présente loi a pour objet de fixer les dispositions applicables à l’industrie cinématographique et notamment celles relatives à la production, à la distribution, à l’exploitation des films cinématographiques et à leur promotion par tous supports … Audiovisuel : toute activité ayant pour objet la production, la distribution et l’exploitation de films cinématographiques sur tous supports d’enregistrement ou de leur diffusion télévisuelle ou sur des plates-formes électroniques, excepté les écrans de cinéma. … Art. 49. — Les investisseurs dans les domaines relevant de l’industrie cinématographique bénéficient des privilèges et des mesures incitatives prévus par la législation et la réglementation en vigueur.

sources.title: HKSAR Government press release, 14 May 2026: Results of final winners of Content Development Scheme for Streaming Platforms announced (issued for the FDC)
sources.said: Four final winners of the Content Development Scheme for Streaming Platforms under the Film Development Fund (FDF) have been selected. Each winner will receive a maximum of $4.5 million for the production of a pilot of their streaming series. … The Scheme, having received over 50 eligible applications, recruited participating teams through a competition to develop content for a series for streaming platforms. Among the applications, 10 projects were shortlisted, and each received a script development fee of $600,000 to $1.2 million to develop a full production proposal and scripts of an entire series. The final four winners out of the 10 shortlisted projects each receive a maximum of $4.5 million to produce a pilot of the series to identify potential platform investors. Together with the script development fee, each final winning team is awarded a total of up to $5.7 million.

sources.title: FDC: Content Development Scheme for Streaming Platforms – Guide to Application
sources.said: 4.1 … (b) each and every producer, director, script supervisor and scriptwriter must be a permanent resident of Hong Kong aged eighteen (18) years or above; … 4.2 The proposed mini-series (“Mini-series”) shall have at least six (6) episodes, with the running time of each episode of at least forty-five (45) minutes. It shall be a fictional narrative (animated series and docuseries not included). … 6.3.3 … ten (10) Applications as Phase 2 projects … will receive a cash prize of a minimum of $600,000 for a six (6)-episode Mini-series, with $100,000 for each episode from the 7th episode up to $1,200,000 being the maximum amount … 6.4.2 … not more than four (4) Mini-series (“Phase 3 Projects”) will be selected. … will receive a cash prize of $4.5 million for producing the Pilot Episodes. … the cash prize shall only be used for production of the Pilot Episodes and shall not cover any other expenses such as promotion and marketing, distribution etc. … 6.5.5 … it can of its own volition seek funding from other investors, financiers and/or streaming platform operators to finance the production of the remaining episodes of the Mini-series. Unless with the approval of the Government, the completed entire series can only be released on streaming platforms which are on the list of streaming platforms to be specified by the Government from time to time and are available to viewers in Hong Kong within the first three (3) years upon the completion of the Pilot Episodes. If the Selected Phase 2 Company secures funding to finance the completion of the entire Mini-series, the entire series shall only be available on streaming platforms on a subscription basis in the first year of release.

items.fact: A tax incentive for theatre production

sources.title: Income Tax Act, Cap. 123 (legislation.mt consolidated, amended to Act III of 2026), art. 56(26A)
sources.said: (26A) (a) An individual who derives income from a full-time or part-time artistic activity shall, unless he opts to have the said income charged to tax at the rates laid down in sub-article (1)(a) or (1)(b), be charged to tax on all such income at the rate of seven point five cents (€0.075) on every euro of the amount of the income so derived net of any deductions allowable in terms of article 14 in respect of expenses incurred in the production thereof. … (b) … income shall be deemed to have been income derived from an artistic activity if it has been so certified by the Arts Council Malta … ‡Applicable from year of assessment 2023. §Applicable from year of assessment 2026. … (c) This sub-article shall be subject to such limitations and conditions as the Minister may prescribe by rules.

sources.title: Fenech & Fenech Advocates (Legal 500, reached from mondaq.com): 7.5% Reduced Tax Rate On Income From Artistic Activities
sources.said: the reduced rate of tax is only applicable to self-employed individuals who generate income from "artistic activities" … actors; artistic directors; … the artistic activities undertaken must be for any of the following "artistic purposes": theatrical, stage, motion picture and TV productions; … The 7.5% reduced rate of tax is only applicable on the first €30,000 turnover (i.e. revenue) generated from artistic activities.
sources.quotes: ITA art. 56(26A) and Arts Council Malta's guidelines (artscouncilmalta.gov.mt, 403 here)

artistIncomeRelief.base: artistic income net of allowable expenses (from YA 2026; gross turnover before)
artistIncomeRelief.on: first EUR 30,000 (guidelines, per the law firm)
artistIncomeRelief.who: self-employed actors, artistic directors, choreographers, writers and others certified by Arts Council Malta
artistIncomeRelief.purposes: theatrical, stage, motion picture and TV productions among them

items.notes: No tax incentive for producing a play was found; the relief lowers the artist's own tax, which a stage actor or director in the engine would keep.

sources.title: Doha Film Institute: Grants (Fall 2026 cycle)
sources.said: We provide creative and financial support, subject to eligibility criteria, for short and feature-length films, as well as TV and web series … TV Fiction & Creative Documentary Series This grant supports independent screenwriters and producers from the MENA region in developing original serialised content for the international audiovisual market. Web Fiction & Creative Documentary Series This grant provides independent directors and producers from the MENA region with funding to produce original serialised content for the web. … The Fall 2026 grants submission opens on the 22nd of June 2026 and closes on the 2nd of July 2026 at 5pm GMT +3.

sources.title: Doha Film Institute: Grants Programme Guidelines, Series (the TV and Web guideline linked from the grants page)
sources.said: 1. Development funding for TV Series: • The Programme defines TV series as serialized content with at least three linear episodes. • An episode is defined as minimum of 26 minutes in duration. • A MENA screenwriter and/or director with previous credits must be attached. • An attached producer with a registered company is strongly preferred at the time of submission. • Rights to the proposal should not be transferred to a broadcaster or VOD platform at the time of submission. 2. Production funding for Web Series: • … at least six linear episodes. • An episode is defined as minimum of 3 minutes in duration. … • The pilot episode for the series must have been completed at the time of submission. • A minimum of 50% of the financing at the time of submission is strongly preferred. … Series Grant Amounts TV Series Development: up to $20,000 Web Series Production: up to $30,000

value.applicant: Qatar and MENA (director's nationality decides); a MENA writer or director with credits attached
value.cycles: two a year (January and July windows)

items.notes: DFI funds only the development of a television series, not its production; no count of applications against grants found.

sources.said: Загальний бюджет ЛОТу — 45,2 млн грн.* Мінімальна сума гранту (не може бути зменшена): 500 тис. грн. Максимальна сума гранту (не може бути збільшена): 3 млн грн. Для ЛОТу передбачено обов’язкове співфінансування у розмірі не менше 20% від бюджету проєкту. … театральні постановки (вистави, п’єси, мюзикли); … перформативні (сценічні) види мистецтва: опера, оперета, балет, мюзикл, драма, перформанс, циркова вистава; … Заявником ЛОТу може бути юридична особа всіх форм власності або фізична особа-підприємець, кожна з яких зареєстрована на території України відповідно до чинного законодавства України не менше, ніж за один рік на дату оголошення конкурсу, за виключенням тимчасово окупованих територій України … Подача проєктної заявки на конкурс: 01.12.2025 – 01.02.2026 … Реалізація проєктів … (але не раніше 01.05.2026 р.) до 30.10.2026.
